title: telemetry event parameters (log_model, register_model, env_pack): bound every value to a known set, None, or bool, and map anything unrecognised to "other"
answers: Why does the log_model telemetry event report flavor as "other" for my custom flavor?
How are register_model telemetry source_scheme and env_pack values recorded when the model URI uses an unusual scheme or a plugin-defined scheme?
I want to add a new telemetry field to an event. Which values are allowed to go into event parameters?
Where is the telemetry flavor or model URI scheme normalized for log_model and register_model?
body:
Path: mlflow/telemetry/events.py:LogModelEvent.parse and RegisterModelEvent.parse turn Model.log and fluent register_model arguments into telemetry params (flavor, registered, env_pack, source_scheme). Flavor goes through events.py:_bound_flavor; the URI scheme is taken with urlparse.
Rule: Telemetry params must be enums, booleans, or None, never free-form or user-identifying text. Map any value outside an explicit set to "other". Use hardcoded sets: mlflow/telemetry/constant.py:KNOWN_FLAVORS for flavors and events.py:_KNOWN_MODEL_URI_SCHEMES for schemes. Do not use the artifact-repository registry for schemes, because plugins can add schemes at runtime and the value would become unbounded. A flavor like "mlflow.sklearn" or "pyfunc.ChatModel" is reduced to its base name before lookup.
Symptom: Without bounding, custom or third-party flavor names and plugin URI schemes would be sent as raw strings in telemetry, and reviewers flagged this as unbounded data.
Constraints: KNOWN_FLAVORS must be edited by hand when a built-in flavor is added or removed. A scheme-less path (for example /tmp/model) maps to "local". A single-slash scheme such as dbfs:/ has a real scheme and is not "local". Existing per-operation events are not changed by this rule.
applies: Any new or changed telemetry event parse() in mlflow/telemetry/events.py that reads user-supplied values such as flavor names, URIs, or registry or plugin names.
says: Usage telemetry records custom model flavors as other instead of their actual name.
Telemetry logging should restrict model storage schemes to predefined values to protect user privacy.
Model registration metrics categorize plugin storage schemes under other in usage reports.
Ensure telemetry events only collect bounded enumerations rather than free-form user strings.
search: In mlflow/telemetry/events.py, LogModelEvent.parse and RegisterModelEvent.parse must constrain all telemetry parameters to booleans, None, or values from hardcoded sets, mapping any unrecognized string to 'other'. Model flavors are validated against mlflow/telemetry/constant.py:KNOWN_FLAVORS after reducing them to base names, and model URI schemes are matched against _KNOWN_MODEL_URI_SCHEMES rather than runtime registries to prevent unbounded plugin values. Scheme-less paths map to 'local' while single-slash schemes like dbfs:/ remain valid schemes. The rule applies to new or modified telemetry parsing in mlflow/telemetry/events.py that handles user-supplied arguments, leaving existing per-operation events unchanged.
